input: Take a beginner's calligraphy class downtown

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Calligraphy spans many styles (Western, brush, copperplate, modern) — knowing which style determines which classes are relevant.
Downtown of which city determines which specific studios and venues to look into.
Whether the user needs a class on a specific date, within a certain timeframe, or on particular days of the week affects which options are viable.
Class prices vary widely; knowing the budget rules out or prioritises certain studios or workshop formats.
Classes can be one-time workshops, multi-week courses, private lessons, or group sessions — the preferred format changes what to search for.
Knowing whether this is for the user alone or with others (a friend, partner, group outing) affects class size requirements and booking logistics.
Understanding the end goal — hobby exploration, a specific project like wedding invitations, or ongoing skill-building — shapes which class depth and curriculum matter most.

gold.taskTitle: Take a beginner calligraphy class downtown
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and attend a beginner-level calligraphy class at a downtown location.

questions.title: Which calligraphy style are you most interested in learning?
questions.description: Identify the specific style — such as modern brush lettering, traditional copperplate, Gothic, or East Asian brush calligraphy — to narrow down relevant class offerings.

questions.title: Which city's downtown are you looking for classes in?
questions.description: Pinpoint the exact city or neighbourhood so that studio and venue searches are geographically accurate.

questions.title: Do you have a target date or timeframe to attend?
questions.description: Determine whether the user has a deadline, a preferred month, or specific days of the week they are available, to filter class schedules accordingly.

questions.title: What is your budget for this class?
questions.description: Establish a price range the user is comfortable with, since beginner workshops can range from free community events to premium private lessons.

questions.title: Do you prefer a one-time workshop or a multi-session course?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants a single drop-in session to try it out, or a structured multi-week course for more sustained learning.

questions.title: Will you be attending alone or with other people?
questions.description: Find out if this is a solo activity or a group outing with friends, a partner, or colleagues, which affects class size needs and group booking requirements.

questions.title: What is your main goal for taking this class?
questions.description: Understand the underlying motivation — casual hobby exploration, a practical project like addressing wedding invitations, or building a long-term skill — to match the right class depth and curriculum.
